messages:
Ana (Sales): Hey team — trying to prep for a POC with FinBank. They want Redwood Private in their AWS VPC. Qs: VPC Peering vs PrivateLink tradeoffs? firewall rules needed? any pricing/entitlement blockers for Dedicated vs Private? Need short answer for RFP.

Raj (Solutions Eng): Short: PrivateLink (AWS NLB + Interface endpoints) is preferred for cross-account secure access, avoids route table changes and doesn't require peering. VPC peering is simpler for same-account but doesn't support transitive routing. Pricing: PrivateLink has hourly endpoint + data processing charges; peering has VPC data transfer costs.

Mei (Networks): For our Private deployment we expose either: 1) PrivateLink interface endpoint per region (recommended); or 2) NAT'd egress through our egress IP ranges if customer prefers outbound only. Required SGs:
- Inbound: allow TCP 443 from customer ENIs (PrivateLink) OR allow from peer VPC CIDR (peering) to the LB/instances.
- Outbound: allow 443 to our collector endpoints for metrics/heartbeats (we can whitelist our IP ranges).

Raj (Solutions Eng): Example SG rule (customer side) -> allow outbound to our endpoints:
```
Type: HTTPS
Protocol: TCP
PortRange: 443
Destination: 13.59.112.0/22  # Redwood Private egress
Description: allow outbound to redwood control plane
```
We don't require any inbound SSH.

Sam (Security): They asked about firewall egress auditing and TLS termination. Confirm: all control plane traffic is TLS 1.2+ and mutual TLS for customer admin APIs? Also need to add: no shared keys in transit and KMS support for keys in private deployments.

Raj (Solutions Eng): Correct. Control plane uses mTLS with client certs when Private is configured. For data plane traffic (model inference), payloads stay within customer VPC if using peering; with PrivateLink, model traffic traverses the interface ENIs into our Private endpoints — still encrypted.

Lia (Customer Engineer): Scheduling a sync with FinBank network team tomorrow 10am PT. I'll bring a slide with: architecture diagrams (peering vs privatelink), sample SG/route entries, and a cost snapshot. @Mei can you add a short CIDR list we can paste into the doc?

Mei (Networks): Pasted CIDRs (for sales doc):
- 13.59.112.0/22
- 34.120.15.0/24
- 52.23.200.0/24
(These are our egress / endpoint ranges per region; we'll update region map in the portal.)

Ana (Sales): Perfect. One more: do we need a VPC endpoint service name or is it on request?

Raj (Solutions Eng): We publish an AWS VPC endpoint service name per deployment. Customer creates interface endpoints pointing to that service. For peering, we provide a peer account ID and a target subnet for our instances.

Sam (Security): For the RFP include: SOC 2 Type II, encryption at rest+in transit, optional Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) via KMS, and firewall whitelist of the CIDRs above. Also call out no plaintext logs leave the VPC unless explicitly enabled.

deploy-bot: Ticket #SB-4921 created for "FinBank Private POC - network checklist" — assignees: Lia, Mei, Raj.

Lia (Customer Engineer): I'll upload the checklist after the call and drop link here.

Ana (Sales): Thanks all — will forward this to their procurement team. :thumbsup:
